svg.title: Batching, concurrency, and reuse
svg.desc: One fabric_exec request branches into four provider reads and joins their results inside the guest. The guest filters results and returns one response. All reads still incur checks. Default concurrency is eight host calls, with a shared queue covering parallel and Promise.all. There are 64 host-call slots but the default audit budget admits only 31 audited calls. One idle compiler per service is reused for 30 seconds and recycled after 250 uses. Discovery is on demand. End-to-end savings have not been established. See docs/diagram-descriptions.md, Efficiency.
svg.text: Example: inspect four known, independent files

g.text: 1. One outer request → four reads
Kiro submits one deterministic fabric_exec.
Each read still receives validation and policy.
Read 1
Read 2
Read 3
Read 4
2. Combine data before returning
map / filter / aggregate inside the guest.
Return selected evidence instead of raw data.
One result for Kiro; fewer outer exchanges.
3. Bound concurrency and total work
Default: 8 simultaneous host calls per execution.
One queue covers parallel and Promise.all.
64 host-call slots; audit budget fits 31 audited calls.
Dependent steps stay ordered; conflicts reject.
4. Reuse compiler setup
At most 1 warm idle compiler per service.
Idle expiry: 30 s. Recycle after 250 uses.
Reuse stable declarations; check every program.
Each execution still gets a fresh QuickJS context.
Discover actions with tools.search / describe.
MCP discovery still follows approval policy.
Costs remain; savings are not yet established.
